subject: social
title: Long Ago and Today
about: Past, present and future, timelines, how everyday life changed from long ago to today, and a few people whose achievements changed how we live. NC 1.H.1.1.
tip: Ask a grandparent to tell him one thing that was different when they were six.

cards.q: What do we call the time that has already happened?
What do we call the time that is happening right now?
What do we call the time that has not happened yet?
Which comes first: yesterday, today or tomorrow?
What do we call a line that shows events in the order they happened?
cards.note: A timeline puts the oldest event first and the newest event last.

cards.q: On a timeline, where is the oldest event?
cards.note: A timeline goes from long ago at the start to now at the end.

cards.q: On a timeline, where is the newest event?
cards.note: The newest event is the one closest to now, so it goes last.

cards.q: Long ago, people rode horses to travel. What do most people travel in today?
cards.note: Cars go much faster than horses.

cards.q: Long ago, people used candles for light at night. What do we use today?
cards.note: Electric lights turn on with a switch.

cards.q: Long ago, people washed clothes by hand. What do many people use today?
cards.note: A washing machine washes many clothes at once.

cards.q: Long ago, kids wrote on small slates. What do kids write on today?
cards.note: A slate was a small board, like a tiny chalkboard.

cards.q: Long ago, people kept food cold with big blocks of ice. What do we use today?
cards.note: A refrigerator keeps food cold all day and all night.

cards.q: Long ago, a letter took many days to arrive. How long does a phone call take to reach someone today?
cards.note: A phone call reaches someone far away right away.

cards.q: Your grandparents are grown-ups now. What were they long ago?
cards.note: Everyone grows and changes over time. Old photos show it.
The Wright brothers flew at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, in 1903.
Before the telephone, people far apart sent letters to talk.

cards.q: Who was the first president of the United States?
cards.note: George Washington was the very first president of our country.

cards.q: Long ago, which president helped end slavery?
cards.note: Abraham Lincoln was president long ago. He helped make slavery against the law so people could be free.

cards.q: Who gave a famous speech about his dream that all people be treated fairly?
cards.note: His famous speech is called I Have a Dream.
